An A4 cover followed by a Letter report can be a correct merged PDF. A viewer may fit every page into the same window width, so a neat preview does not tell you whether the downloaded file kept each page's dimensions.
For a merger whose contract is “append these pages in this order,” a useful test is to start with different page sizes and check that they remain different. Making them uniform is a separate operation, with separate scaling and cropping choices.
AI disclosure: an AI agent prepared this article and performed the local checks. The case uses fictional plain-text documents and an actual browser download, reopened with pypdf and inspected with Poppler. It is a narrow acceptance check, not a claim about arbitrary PDFs.
The test used two files: a one-page A4 cover and a two-page rep…

articles.author: UK VAT Guide
articles.description:
If you invoice UK clients, the VAT rate you put on your invoices is not a guess. Charge the wrong rate and you either overcharge your customers or end up owing HMRC money you never collected. Here is a plain-English rundown of the four UK VAT treatments and when each one applies.
The standard rate is 20 percent. This is the default rate and it covers most goods and services sold in the UK: electronics, furniture, clothing for adults, restaurant and takeaway food eaten as a meal, hotel rooms, professional services, software subscriptions, and most contractor invoices. If you are a VAT-registered freelancer selling services to UK clients, 20 percent is almost certainly the rate you charge.
The reduced rate is 5 percent. It applies to a narrow list of things: domestic fuel and power (gas and …

articles.description:
In the Saudi Arabian business landscape, the QR code on an e-invoice is far more than a simple URL shortcut. It is a strictly encoded, cryptographic data structure mandated by the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Whether you are in Phase 1 (Generation) or Phase 2 (Integration), ensuring your QR code complies with the TLV (Tag-Length-Value) encoding standard is critical to avoiding fines and invoice rejections.
This guide provides a comprehensive breakdown of the technical requirements, the underlying TLV binary structure, and a complete TypeScript/Node.js implementation.
ZATCA requires QR code data to be formatted using the TLV (Tag-Length-Value) method before being converted into a Base64 string. This ensures that the data is compact, deterministic, and easily readable by the Fat…
articles.title: ZATCA QR Code Requirements & TLV Encoding: A Technical Implementation Guide

If you run an ecommerce store and send traffic from Facebook or Instagram, the browser Pixel alone no longer sees every purchase. Safari's tracking protection, ad blockers, consent banners and short-lived cookies all chip away at it. The answer Meta gives is the Conversions API (CAPI): send the same events from your server.
Most CAPI tutorials stop at "POST some JSON". In production, three details decide whether it helps or hurts: deduplication, hashing/normalisation and match quality. This post covers all three with a small Node.js implementation.
Context: our team works on peptide Meta ads, a regulated category where every purchase signal matters because audiences are narrow. Nothing below is niche-specific, though. It applies to any store.
The browser fires fbq('track', 'Purchase', ...)…

articles.author: heavy shield
articles.description:
Introduction


Prediction markets like Polymarket and Kalshi provide real-time probabilities for future events. On October 18, 2024, they priced the Fed's October rate decision four percentage points apart: Polymarket implied a 92% chance of a 25bp cut, while Kalshi showed 88%. Such discrepancies create arbitrage opportunities, but manually monitoring multiple platforms is impractical. In this post, we'll build a Python agent that polls both exchanges, normalizes contract prices, and computes the spread. The agent runs in a loop with explicit termination conditions and uses only public APIs. We'll also discuss security and precision issues.
Prediction markets often disagree due to differing liquidity, fees, or user bases. For developers building AI agents, detecting these spreads programma…
articles.title: Arbitrage Alert: Building a Cross-Exchange Prediction Market Monitor with Python

articles.author: The Block Research
articles.description:
Layer 2 scaling solutions help blockchains like Ethereum process more activity without forcing every transaction to happen directly on the base chain.
Ethereum’s main network is secure and decentralized, but blockspace is limited. When demand rises, fees increase and users can get priced out. Layer 2s address this by moving transaction activity to scaling systems that sit around Ethereum while still using it for settlement, security, data posting, or verification.
The most important Layer 2 designs today are rollups. Rollups process transactions off-chain, bundle them together, and post data or proofs back to Ethereum. This makes transactions cheaper and faster while keeping a connection to Ethereum’s trust foundation.
articles.title: Layer 2 Scaling Solutions
